---
title: "Methods"
---

## How a study is run

Every study follows the same contract, so that any rule can be tested on equal
footing with any other:

- The hypothesis is written down before the pipeline runs: the event series,
  the rule, the time window, the expected direction, the test, the significance
  level and the correction for multiple comparisons.
- Planetary positions come from the Swiss Ephemeris, with the ayanamsa and the
  node model stated in every output.
- Event catalogues are declustered where the events cluster (aftershocks), and
  every dataset is recorded with its source, licence and SHA-256 hash (see
  [Data](data.qmd)).
- Comparisons use event-rate ratios with confidence intervals and Molchan
  diagrams against a time-random baseline. Null distributions preserve
  autocorrelation (block bootstrap or phase randomisation).
- Multiplicity is corrected across every rule tested (Benjamini-Hochberg), and
  effect sizes are reported whether or not they reach significance.
- Market series are checked for stationarity before any Granger-type test, and
  forecasts are evaluated walk-forward on a held-out period.
- Every figure and number in a paper is produced by the study's scripts with a
  fixed seed and a recorded data hash.

## Working expectations

The project owner's current expectation, recorded as a hypothesis to be tested
rather than a premise: planetary motion is smooth and deterministic in every
ayanamsa and every divisional chart, while earthquakes, floods and prices are
bursty and partly random, so if a relationship exists it is more likely to
appear as a change in the *rate* or *conditions* of events during a
configuration than as a point prediction.

This is one expectation among others that astrologers may hold (for example,
that specific transits to a national chart coincide with specific event
types). The methods above are chosen so that any of these can be tested on
equal footing: event-rate ratios with confidence intervals, Molchan diagrams
against a time-random baseline, declustered catalogues, multiplicity correction
across every rule tested, and effect sizes reported whether or not they reach
significance. The studies answer the expectation; it does not decide them.

## Methods in practice

The contract above is implemented once, in `vedic_astrology_core.stats`
(`libs/vedic_astrology_core/stats/`), and every study calls it instead of
writing its own tests:

| Step | Module | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Stationarity gate | `stationarity` | ADF and KPSS; applies one difference or log-difference and refuses the test if the series is still non-stationary |
| Null surrogates | `nulls` | circular shift of the indicator (offset at least the longest period), stationary block bootstrap, phase randomisation; all seeded through `np.random.default_rng(seed)` |
| Permutation test | `permutation` | p = (n_extreme + 1) / (n + 1), effect size against the null and a block-bootstrap interval |
| Multiplicity | `multiplicity` | Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli or Bonferroni across every (rule, target) pair |
| Event rates | `rates` | rate ratio with an exact Poisson interval, tested against circular shifts |
| Molchan | `molchan` | alarm fraction on the time axis, binomial bounds for N events, area skill score, time-random reference |
| Granger-type tests | `granger` | astro series as exogenous regressors in an ADL with Newey-West errors and a fixed lag set |
| Out of sample | `walk_forward` | time split with a frozen confirmation period; Hansen's SPA test for best-rule claims |
| Provenance | `manifest`, `plots` | `manifest.json` (data SHA-256, commit, seed, ephemeris model, ayanamsa, node model) and a footer on every figure |

The earthquake study is the first study rebuilt on it. Its pre-registration
is `studies/earthquake/hypothesis.yaml` (region polygon, Mw homogenisation,
completeness, two declustering methods, thirteen enumerated indicators, a
10,000-draw circular-shift null, Benjamini-Yekutieli across 26 tests, and a
1976-2010 / 2011-2026 split). One command,
`python studies/earthquake/scripts/pipeline.py --seed 42`, writes every table
and figure and the `results.json` from which the paper's Results and
Discussion are generated. The first run found no configuration that passed the
family correction; the paper reports the rate ratios and intervals for all of
them.
